# Linux Native Port Plan

Updated: 2026-10-15

## Goal

Deliver a native Linux client for Prime World without Wine, while keeping the Windows client buildable and functionally intact.

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- Do not remove or regress the Windows client path.
- Keep Linux-only behavior behind `__linux__`, Linux-specific targets, or bootstrap-only compile definitions.
- Prefer cross-platform fixes when they are low-risk and do not change Windows behavior.
- Batch work into larger chunks and keep this file current so progress does not depend on chat history.
- User instruction (2026-10-10): commit and push after each completed, verified chunk. Each commit needs a descriptive body and `Co-authored-by: OpenAI ChatGPT <noreply@openai.com>`. This supersedes historical notes below that left work uncommitted for manual review. Do not commit crash dumps or generated test/build output.
- Version native-port checkpoints through `LinuxBootstrap/VERSION` and matching annotated `linux-native-v<version>` tags. Both Linux CMake projects consume that version. Keep shared `Src/Version.h` network/replay values, pinned third-party versions, and the C ABI protocol version independent; bumping them merely to label port work would change compatibility contracts. The native UI/runtime checkpoint is `0.1.0`; the isolated Ruffle adapter adds features in `0.2.0`.

- Previous continuation (2026-10-09, one bounded Unicode-safety chunk): hardened the shared `NStr::UTF8ToUnicode` / `UnicodeToUTF8` Linux implementations used by the newly promoted production caption path. The old decoder walked beyond the end of truncated input; the regression executable reproduced exit `139` on a truncated two-byte sequence, with core dumps disabled. It also reproduced lost supplementary characters and acceptance of malformed encodings. Linux now uses the already-linked native `iconv` service with explicit byte bounds, signed-length allocation guards, and scalar-value validation in both directions. Invalid/truncated UTF-8, surrogate code points, negative wide values, and out-of-range scalars clear the output rather than returning a partial caption. Valid conversions remain locale-independent and preserve embedded NULs and supplementary characters. Windows converter bodies are unchanged; preprocessed non-Linux bodies were compared against `HEAD` and matched exactly.

## What Is Not Done Yet

- A shippable playable client is still blocked by the Direct3D 9-centered production renderer and by scene/client/runtime coupling that remains behind the Linux bootstrap backend.
- The current Linux executable enters a native loaded world and exercises real simulation, commands, UI, and renderer-owned content, but it is still a bootstrap-integrated subset rather than the complete production client loop and transport stack.
- Full production gameplay rendering, complete UI/localization, audio, networking, and final client runtime integration are not running yet. The shipped XDB/Lua starting lobby and hero lobby now render through the OpenGL UI renderer, and the production loading layout creates the real `FlashContainer2`, loads `pwl.swf`, and submits it through native OpenGL. Both starting and hero menus now default to their shipped XDB/Lua presentation; the old bridges are opt-in through `--bootstrap-legacy-lobby-overlay` and `--bootstrap-legacy-hero-overlay`. The first visible 3D is an auto-rotating, zoomable, tiltable, pannable, mouse/key-controlled selected-map tactical preview with real sampled terrain heightmap geometry, authored terrain-layer mask coloring, authored `NDb::AdvMapWaterZone` water overlays, real `DBNatureMap` road polylines, authored script/camera guide overlays, authored point-light range markers, real `MapStartInfo` hero start-slot assignment rings/columns, terrain-followed team-route overlays from start slots to allied lanes/objectives plus A/B lane corridors, capped real `NDb::Terrain::geometry.terrainElements` mesh payloads, capped real selected-map static and animated scene-object meshes, plus a textured selected-hero preview through maintained `Render::SkeletalMesh` / `Render::StaticMesh` queue APIs. The loaded `PFWorld` create-game smoke allocates real lane and neutral creep gameplay objects from DB-backed spawners, steps common-creep movement, and feeds the OpenGL tactical preview with live heroes, creeps, objectives, and moving units. This remains a constrained bootstrap renderer: full materials/shaders/animation graphs, uncapped production scene rendering, client-owned hero/creep scene objects, production cameras/effects, complete in-game UI, sound, transport, and session lifecycle are still open.

## Main Remaining Milestones

The startup/render milestones below are historical foundations already demonstrated by the current native client. The authoritative evidence is in the current batch above. For the playable-game goal, merely launching and moving a hero is insufficient: the remaining acceptance must cover an ordinary local match through combat, progression, death/respawn and actual match completion, with usable original UI and no diagnostic actions required. Native finish handling is a confirmed missing connection as of C56. Visual parity, effects, audio, stability and an actual Windows build remain separate acceptance work.

### 1. Renderer escape hatch

Create a Linux-safe null-render or minimal renderer path that lets the real client startup move past the current Direct3D 9 wall.

Success condition:
- real client startup goes further than the current bootstrap shell without including `d3d9.h` on the Linux path

### 2. First real client startup on Linux

Move from shell/bootstrap behavior into more of the actual client runtime, even if visual output is incomplete.

Success condition:
- Linux client enters the real client loop with native startup, real runtime objects, and no D3D dependency on the Linux path

### 3. First in-game render

Bring up the first native Linux-rendered scene, even if minimal or visually wrong.

Success condition:
- map scene renders on Linux with enough runtime integration to observe live world state

### 4. First playable local match

Reach a playable local game on Linux with input, world simulation, basic UI visibility, and stable rendering.

Success condition:
- launch a local match and control a hero natively on Linux

### 5. Stabilization and parity

Fix correctness, UI gaps, audio, launcher integration, and wider gameplay/client regressions.

Success condition:
- Linux client is stable enough to ship publicly without breaking the Windows client

The real renderer/backend path is still centered on Direct3D 9 and Windows-specific render infrastructure, especially:

- `Src/Render/renderer.h`

### Secondary blocker

Scene and client runtime code still pull render-side types too early. The Linux path needs a cleaner seam between gameplay/runtime code and scene/render code.

### Current render frontier

Latest B13 renderer boundary (C21-C23, C28): actual native StaticMesh/Batch/SmartRenderer draws translate the shipped BasicFX Simple, AdditiveOpacity and BlendOpacity bytecode pairs (0/12/24) through the pinned MojoShader subset. One atomic family load per context supplies fixed CPU tickets; per-material switching does not compile/link. Constant opacity uses the authored pin and original PS c6 opacity*masterOpacity, independently of blend mode; Simple ignores the product. Constant materials support final-alpha GEQUAL cutouts, optional backface culling and the six original non-Off blend factors, with explicit context ownership, checked inputs and restored host GL state. Non-Off draws preserve destination alpha/depth and require GL4 or ARB_draw_buffers_blend indexed entrypoints; unavailable capability rejects blending without disabling GL3.3 opaque draws. Eligible terrain-element/static-object batches share a retained-owner, original BatchQueue back-to-front pass after opaque unit meshes and before overlays; character attachments have a separate view-local pass. Sorting uses checked transformed authored bounds, not submission order. The shipped Flat03 opacity slot now draws its original geometry, texture and BlendOpacity 1.1 material; its unsupported BasicMaterial sibling is not included in that proof. This is a selected production-shader path, not full material/scene parity: skeletal transparency, particles, animated constants, emissive/runtime fade overrides, other permutations, lighting/shadows and mip chains remain outside it. Water/road visualization remains an early underlay, and unsupported materials keep the existing immediate preview. Authored alpha-tested candidate definitions found so far belong to animated assets; the static-engine cutout fixture combines shipped geometry and texture for verification rather than claiming those complete animated effects are ported. The top-of-file checkpoint entries are authoritative over older compile-coverage descriptions below.

- `Terrain/TerrainMaterialCache.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainHeightManager.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainLayerManager.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainTextureCache.cpp`, `Terrain/NatureMapVisual.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainElement.cpp`, `Terrain/Terrain.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainCollision.cpp`, `Terrain/TerrainGeometryManager.cpp`, `Terrain/BezierSurface.cpp`, and `Terrain/NatureAttackSpace.cpp` are no longer outside the maintained probe. The render-probe-specific `PW_LINUX_TERRAIN_RUNTIME_PROBE` split in `Terrain.h` now lets the real terrain runtime compile on Linux while gameplay bootstrap keeps the lightweight terrain surface.
- `Terrain/UberElement.cpp` is still outside the maintained probe, but it is explicitly deprecated in-tree (`#error "This file was deprecated 28.05.2008"`) and depends on missing retired headers (`DummyElement.h`), so it should stay out unless some content unexpectedly revives it.
- `Scene/TimeCtrlSceneComponent.cpp` still targets removed DB/runtime APIs on Windows, which is why it remains excluded from the normal source list. For Linux maintenance it now has a probe-only null-render stub, so it is no longer an open portability blocker.

## Current Effort Estimate

There is no defensible current percentage or release date. The previous `60-70% remaining` estimate predates the current gameplay, HUD and original-graph work and must not be used as a current assessment. Batch checkpoint counts measure completed work, not a percentage of a playable release. Track the concrete full-match acceptance and parity gaps above instead.

## Working Rules For Future Updates

- Update this file after each substantial chunk, not after every tiny edit.
- Record the latest verified build/run commands and latest verified log path.
- When a blocker changes, move it here immediately so the next session does not need to reconstruct context from chat.
- Prefer moving the maintained Linux gameplay probe deeper before touching risky shared code blindly.
- Use this document as the source of truth for port status, not chat memory.
